chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Chick Webb's drum equipment: tympani heads, sticks, cymbals
summary: Webb used xylophone and tympani, tympani heads on his drums, carefully chosen sticks and Zildjian cymbals, and pioneered the hi-hat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: What percussion instruments did Chick Webb play, Teddy? Did he play tympani or --
Oh, he could play tympani.
What about the xylophone?
He played the xylo -- The picture I showed you he was playing
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
the xylophone. Chick was one of the few drummers -- I think he started this off and all the drummers picked it up.
He used to use -- People wondered why his drums used to sound different from the other drummers. Well, Chick would use like on his drumhead, he would use like tympani heads.
See, he used tympani heads on his drums, you know. And he was very choosy about his cymbals and sticks.
He would go into Manny's for drum sticks -- he'd go through maybe two dozen sticks and probably come out with four that he liked.
And he go back every week and he go downtown and he buy four -- four or five or a half a dozen more.
He'd go through a whole stack of sticks, feeling them and balancing them -- see if they had the right balance. And he would work on these sticks.
And he'd go up to Zildjian's, the big cymbal people who make these big cymbals.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Zildjian's?

Yeah. He'd go up there -- and he knew this guy. And every time he went up to Boston, he'd go out to whatever factory was there and he'll pick up a cymbal. He was the first one that made the hi-hat. You know, those cymbals (inaudible). He was the first one -- really be the first one to effect the hi-hat in the cymbals. He could hit cymbals, slant off them with the sticks and make them ring. Get more sound out of them than any other drummer that you ever heard of. You could hear the cymbal make the whole (inaudible) sound-jaroom, they just shatter, you know, like the whole -- just lift the whole band up. Like he was hitting a tympani or something. I guess like he had those tympani heads on, he could drum. His drum sound deeper and heavier. Sound like music. Would sound like, boom, boom, boom. He'd get a lot of sound out those drums.

He used tympani heads on a snare?
No. (Inaudible) good snare heads, you know. It was only on the drums that were used.
The pedals -- he was very -- the pedals had to be something special to him. He had very fine pedals. The best.
He had one of those large bass drums.
Yeah. (Inaudible) set (inaudible). Regular set, yeah. At that time, they had the regular -- you know, the regular big sets. Now they use a little smaller bass drums.
But I think a lot of the guys after that began to use tympani heads on their drums. (inaudible).
